A tumultuous disturbance of the public peace by a large group of people, often involving violence or damage to property.

examples.text: The protests began peacefully but turned into riots after several days.

glosses: A wide and unconstrained variety.

examples.text: In summer this flower garden is a riot of colour.

glosses: To create or take part in a riot; to raise an uproar or sedition.

examples.text: The nuclear protesters rioted outside the military base.

examples.text: Now he exact of all, wastes in delight, / Riots in pleasure, and neglects the law.

glosses: To cause to riot; to throw into a tumult.

An excessively violent or vicious attack; an atrocity.

examples.text: There the cause of death was soon ascertained ; the victim of this daring outrage had been stabbed to death from ear to ear with a long, sharp instrument, in shape like an antique stiletto, which […] was subsequently found under the cushions of the hansom.[…]

glosses: An offensive, immoral or indecent act.
The resentful, indignant, or shocked anger aroused by such acts.
A destructive rampage.
